3. Facts, in short, are that case holding was  leased out on October 26, 1962 to one S.K. Rezvi, who died1965 leaving behind wife- Behar Am (Respondent No.4) and 2 minor final sons-Zakir Hossein Rezvi, and Iftekhar Rezvi. The mother of the minors was appointed their guardian. On mortgaging the property loan was obtained from the House Building Finance Corporation and the heirs of S.K. Rezvi contacted building in the land got by lease. The Respondent No. 4 entered into an agreement j with the Respondent No. 1 herein to sell the land with the building of the holding in question. Since the Respondent No, 4 failed to execute deed of transfer, the Respondent No. 1 filed Title Suit No. 3 of 1979 which was later on renumbered as Title Suit No. 1375 of 1981. The said suit was decreed and a kabala was obtained through Court on January 3, 1984. 

 7. The learned Additional Attorney General submits that this Division erred in dismissing the leave petition placing reliance on a decree obtained in the suit for specific performance of contract to sell the property in question and as such the judgment and order of this Division rejecting the leave petition requires review since the said judgment and order is contrary to the settled principle of law that decree in a suit for specific performance of contract to sell land is not a bar in listing a property as an abandoned property under the provisions of section 5 of the Ordinance No. 54 of 1985. The learned Additional Attorney General also submits that High court Division erred in setting aside the judgment of the Court of Settlement which is a well reasoned one and that said judgment was made upon consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case in the background of the papers and the evidence brought on record by the parties. 

 8. The contention of the learned Additional Attorney General that this Division in rejecting the leave petition based its judgment on the decree obtained in a suit for specific performance of contract to sell the property in question is not correct. This Division considered the fact that one of the heirs of the original allottee appeared before the court and deposed in support of the fact that she and her sons at no point of time left Bangladesh and that she obtained Nationality Certificate from the competent authority. The Court of Settlement did not consider this vital aspect of the case in its correct perspective. The other contention that judgment of the Court of Settlement ought not to have been set aside by the High Court Division since the same has been made upon consideration of the materials on record is also of no substance since the important fact i.e. presence of the heirs of the allottee in Bangladesh at all material time has not been properly considered by the Court of Settlement. No material was placed on record from the side of the petitioner, in support of considering and listing the property as an abandoned property and as such as the listing of the property was not legal the High Court Division was quite legal in setting aside the judgment of the Court of Settlement rejecting the prayer of the Respondent No. 1 for releasing the property from the list of abandoned buildings. The respondent Nos. 1 and 4 have sufficiently discharged the onus as requires by sec-tion 5(2) of Ordinance No. 54 of 1985.
